title: tensor-chunk-sensitivity-and-micro-schedule-latency-sweep
content:
Summary:

Short: micro-benchmark sweep to understand how fine-grained tensor chunking and the runtime's micro-scheduler interact to affect tail latency (p50/p95/p99) for medium-length inference (2-4k tokens) across multi-GPU nodes. We observed non-monotonic latency behavior when chunk size < 32 KB for certain attention kernels; hypothesis: packetization + NCCL fragmentation + scheduler wakeups create microbursts.

Background / motivation:
- Prior tests focused on coarse-grained batching and broad NCCL pacing knobs. Those experiments left a gap: how does splitting big matmul outputs into small device-to-device transfers (tensor chunking) interact with our micro-scheduler and GPU kernel launch timing?
- On inference workloads with variable sequence lengths, runtime splits KV cache updates and attention key/value tensors into chunks to overlap comm+compute. But chunk size is heuristically chosen; we need empirical guidance.

Goal:
- Produce actionable guidance for default chunk sizes and micro-scheduler parameters (polling intervals, coalescing windows) in the serving runtime. Identify pathological cases and propose mitigations (coalesce threshold, packetization alignment, NCCL buffer sizing).

Hypotheses:
1) Very small chunk sizes (<= 32 KB) increase p95/p99 latency due to NIC/PCIe/NVLink packet overhead and increased NCCL op count, causing more host/GPU context switches and kernel launches.
2) For medium chunk sizes (64 KB - 512 KB) we hit a sweet spot: enough concurrency to hide compute without overwhelming interconnect.
3) Large chunk sizes (> 2 MB) increase tail latency when sequence variability forces straggler chunks; also harms prefix caching reuse.
4) Inter-node vs intra-node: intra-node (NVLink) shows less penalty for smaller chunks up to a point; cross-node performance cliff appears when chunk count triggers many small NCCL collectives and network MTU effects.

Testbed / HW:
- 1 node: 8x A100 SXM4 (NVLink)
- 2 node: 4x A100 NVLink per node, nodes connected over 100GbE (RoCEv2)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch chunking-experiments @ PR-1412 (see linked PR)
- Models: 13B transformer distilled toy model (attention matrix sizes representative of 8192 hidden vs 4k seq), and a 70B-ish config simulated by synthetic kernels to stress large KV volume.
- Measurement: synthetic inference driver that drives variable sequence lengths [512, 1024, 2048, 4096], and logs per-request timeline (host enqueue, kernel-start, kernel-end, comm-start, comm-end, response-ready). Also end-to-end latencies and per-token generation times. Tracing via LTTng + CUPTI + NCCL logging enabled.

Experiment matrix (representative):
- chunk_size_bytes: [8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, 128k, 256k, 512k, 1M, 2M]
- micro_scheduler_coalesce_ms: [0 (no coalesce), 0.2, 0.5, 1.0]
- concurrency_mode: [continuous-batching, fixed-batch, pipeline-interleave]
- network_topology: [intra-node (NVLink), cross-node (RoCE)]
- sequence_len: [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]
- runs: 5 samples per cell, warmup 200 requests, measure next 2000

Quicknotes on knobs we changed in runtime:
- chunker: splits tensors along last dim into chunk_size_bytes approximate chunks (may vary because tensor element sizes matter)
- micro-scheduler: coalesce window that holds pending small transfers and issues one aggregated D2D op up to MAX_COALESCE_BYTES
- NCCL tuning: we kept default for baseline, added runs with NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1 for some cells

Key observations (high level):
1) p50 agnostic, p95/p99 sensitive: Changing chunk size had minor effect on median but large effect on p95/p99. For 2048 and 4096 sequence lengths, 16k and 32k chunk sizes had 30-120% higher p99 vs 128k baseline.
2) Nonlinear cliff crossing: under cross-node runs, when chunk count > ~80 per collective, we saw a sharp step increase in tail latency — matches NCCL behavior where many small ops cause serialization/queueing on network.
3) Coalescing helps but is delicate: enabling a 0.5 ms coalesce window reduced p99 by ~40% for 16k chunks, but added ~1-2 ms to median for small sequences. So coalescing is tradeoff (better tail vs slightly higher median).
4) NVLink intra-node is forgiving: up to ~64k chunks per tensor, intra-node p99 stays flat; cross-node shows penalty earlier (~32k).
5) NCCL async progress reduces host-side stalls but increases GPU-side queuing leading to similar net p99; mixed results — requires per-topology tuning.

Representative numbers (selected cells):
- 2048 seq, cross-node, chunk=16k, coalesce=0: p50=18.2 ms, p95=42.3 ms, p99=89.7 ms
- 2048 seq, cross-node, chunk=128k, coalesce=0: p50=18.0 ms, p95=23.6 ms, p99=28.1 ms
- 2048 seq, cross-node, chunk=16k, coalesce=0.5 ms: p50=19.3 ms, p95=27.4 ms, p99=41.2 ms
- 4096 seq, intra-node, chunk=32k, coalesce=0: p50=32.1 ms, p95=58.8 ms, p99=67.0 ms
- 4096 seq, cross-node, chunk=512k, coalesce=0: p50=34.0 ms, p95=36.2 ms, p99=45.9 ms

Trace snippets (host timeline simplified):
- Bad case (many small chunks):
  host enqueue -> kernelA start -> kernelA end -> submit D2D chunk1 -> submit D2D chunk2 -> ... chunkN -> host busy poll -> kernelB start
  Observed long gaps between kernelA end and kernelB start due to many small NCCL ops and host poll stalls.

- Good case (coalesce or larger chunk):
  host enqueue -> kernelA start -> kernelA end -> submit aggregated D2D -> kernelB start (overlap improved)

Analysis / root causes (working):
- Packetization + ring traversal: cross-node small NCCL collectives cause many small packets, incurring software overhead on NIC (RoCE) and CPU handling.
- Host polling and kernel launch overhead: each small comm completion triggers scheduler wakeups leading to more frequent kernel submissions and context switches.
- Edge-case with CUDA streams ordering: when chunk_count is large, ordering constraints cause kernel launches to serialize in ways we don't expose in profiler; we saw stream stalls in CUPTI timelines.
- Retry/backoff in upper layers: for cross-node when streams hit network congestion, NCCL does transient retries which amplify tail.

Immediate recommendations (runtime defaults):
1) Default chunk size: 128 KB for cross-node; 64 KB for intra-node (NVLink) as safe defaults. Rationale: tradeoff between concurrency and per-op overhead.
2) Enable micro-scheduler coalesce window default 0.5 ms for cross-node clusters; 0.2 ms for intra-node. Allow cluster-level override in config.
3) Add automatic detection: if chunk_count per collective > 64 and topology==cross-node, raise coalesce aggressively and increase NCCL buffer sizes.
4) Expose a per-deployment heuristic that chooses chunk size by model footprint and median sequence length rather than a one-size-fits-all value.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Interaction with quantized kernels: do int8 kernels change the sweet spot because compute time per chunk reduces? Hypothesis: with faster compute, comm becomes dominant and larger chunks preferred.
- Impact of RoCE MTU tuning and NIC coalescing: repeat cross-node tests with different MTU settings and enable NIC-level coalescing to see net effect.
- Observe behavior when real user traffic mixes sequences (not synthetic fixed-length workload) — bimodal distributions might reveal new pathological cases.
- Tune NCCL communicator segmentation parameters (if available) to reduce op count on rings. Need NCCL upstream discussion.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add automated config heuristic in runtime (owner: Tomás Rivera; due: 2024-09-18)
- [ ] Run quantized-kernel runs (owner: Megan Liu; due: 2024-09-25)
- [ ] Synthetic mixed-length trace replay and tail analysis (owner: Samir Khan; due: 2024-09-30)
- [ ] File NCCL issue with reproduction case (owner: Asha Patel; due: 2024-09-10)
- [ ] Add microtrace view to Console docs showing chunk counts and coalesce windows (owner: docs team)

Notes to self / messy observations:
- We saw a weird run where 32k chunks on cross-node had better p99 than 64k; likely measurement noise plus NCCL scheduling nondeterminism. Re-run with pinned cpus and perf counters.
- CUPTI traces show many tiny API events; need to aggregate at the driver layer to reduce noise in our dashboards.

References and links:
- PR with code changes and test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1412
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-3721 — chunking sensitivity epic
- Kernel-level traces: s3://internal-traces/chunking/2024-08-23.tar.gz (internal)

Bottom line (tl;dr): avoid tiny chunk sizes for cross-node collectives; prefer ~128KB baseline, use micro-coalescing windows to reduce p99, and add heuristics that tune chunk sizes per deployment and model. This yields significant tail-latency improvements with minor median impact.
